comments.author: @leechumbley5440
comments.text: What an amazing video. Fascinating to learn more about Stanley’s expeditions. I’ve read Heart of Darkness, but you point out that Conrad’s Congo is absent of people, Amazing to learn that the river is a speciation barrier – bonobos to the south, chimpanzees to the north, and never the twain shall meet (except in periods of extreme dryness every couple of hundred million years. Interesting to learn that Dunlop invented pneumatic tyres and 13 years later 1/10 of the world’s rubber came from here, but at a horrendous cost in cruelty. Patrice Lumumba was a good man who got in the way of greed of the extractive industrialists, and western media bought and enabled the story of his being a dangerous hothead. Sad to learn about Congolese king Alfonso’s lament to Lisbon, ignored much like Comissioner Lin’s letter to Queen Victoria about the Chinese opium trade – got in the way of profit. Interesting to learn how the 2 capitals got their names - Kinshasa from a local word for market, Brazzaville from de Brazza. The blind fish, the world's largest peat bed - so many things to learn.
